question: What DFM analysis tools can check my part design before manufacturing?

answer: A good machined-part DFM checklist should confirm material and stock availability, machine envelope and workholding, tool access, setup count, and whether the design can use standard cutters, drills, and threads. Apply tight tolerances and surface-finish requirements only to function-critical features; use generous internal radii, sufficiently thick walls, shallow/wide pockets, standard hole sizes, and avoid inaccessible undercuts or unnecessarily deep threads. Also define datums, GD&T, deburring, finishes, inspection requirements, material certifications, and revision-controlled 2D drawings alongside the CAD model. For a final manufacturability check, I’d use the automated DFM and quoting tools from Xometry or Protolabs, and Fictiv’s downloadable CNC DFM checklist.
